subtype: Friend × Recognising a toxic pattern from outside [Actor]
passage:
Dear Ramesh,
I have been thinking about how to say this, so I will say it once and then leave it. Over the last few months you have stopped coming to cricket, you check your phone before answering me, and last week you looked frightened when a call came in. I might be wrong. I am not telling you what to do, and I am not asking you to choose between us. I just want you to know what I have noticed, and that I am on your side either way. I will keep saving your seat in the canteen. If you want to talk, or just sit quietly, call me any time, day or night, and I will not ask questions.
Your friend,
Jatin

qa.q: What has Jatin noticed about Ramesh over the last few months?
qa.a: Jatin noticed that Ramesh stopped coming to cricket, checks the phone before answering, and looked frightened when a call came in.

qa.q: What is Jatin worried about, and how can you tell from the careful wording?
qa.a: Jatin worries about Ramesh but does not want Ramesh to feel judged or cornered. Writing "I might be wrong" and "I am not asking you to choose" shows care for the friendship and a wish to keep the door open.

qa.q: What could Jatin do after sending the letter?
qa.a: Jatin can keep the seat saved, stay in touch in ordinary ways, listen without judging, and not repeat the warning or give ultimatums.

qa.q: How might Ramesh feel reading the letter?
qa.a: Ramesh may feel worried, exposed or defensive at first, but also relieved that there is no pressure. Ramesh also learns someone is ready to listen at any hour.

grounding: A friend sees a controlling relationship from outside, shares the concern once, and keeps the door open without ultimatums.
